summary.text: Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because it is moving.
It equals the work needed to speed the object up from rest, and the same amount is done when it slows to a stop.
Kinetic energy can be passed to other objects or turned into other forms such as heat, gravitational energy or electricity.

facts.label: Clay experiment
facts.value: Penetration depth rose with speed squared

items.prompt: A cyclist coasts up a hill until she stops at the top. Where has most of her motion energy gone?

options.label: Into gravitational potential energy she can release going down
Into chemical energy stored in her muscles
Into thermal energy that leaves for good
Into nothing, since it vanished at the stop

items.explain: The kinetic energy has largely been converted to gravitational potential energy, which can be released by freewheeling down.

items.prompt: A cyclist squeezes her brakes to stop on a flat road. Where does her motion energy go?

options.label: Into stored energy in the road
Into heat produced by friction
Into extra speed for the bicycle
Into chemical energy in the brakes

items.explain: Braking dissipates the kinetic energy through friction as heat.

items.prompt: One cyclist coasts downhill with a dynamo on a wheel; another has none. Why is the first slower at the bottom?

options.label: The dynamo adds extra weight that cancels gravity
Dynamos remove speed by pushing the air
Some of the energy was diverted into electricity
Hills are steeper for cyclists using dynamos

items.explain: The bicycle travels slower because some of the energy has been diverted into electrical energy.

items.prompt: A passenger sits still on a moving train. A student says her kinetic energy is one definite number. What is wrong with that?

options.label: It changes with the observer's frame of reference
It is always zero for anyone sitting still
It is the same for every observer you pick
It depends only on how heavy she happens to be

items.explain: Kinetic energy depends on the relationship between the object and the observer's frame of reference, so it is not invariant.

items.prompt: Weights were dropped into clay from various heights. How did the dent depth relate to the impact speed?

options.label: It grew in simple proportion to the speed
It stayed the same for every speed
It shrank as the speed rose
It grew with the square of the speed

items.explain: Penetration depth was proportional to the square of impact speed, supporting the relation of energy to mass times speed squared.

items.prompt: Why do spacecraft returning from orbit get so hot?

options.label: Their engines run hotter on the way down
Some of their motion energy turns into heat
They have stored extra heat from space
Gravity heats up anything that falls

items.explain: Friction becomes apparent at re-entry, where some kinetic energy is converted to heat.
